intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene (606621) on chromosome 3q13.12-q13.13.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we report on a unique consanguineous family with 3 affected siblings with an unclassified OFDS subtype with short stature and brachymesophalangia, harboring a homozygous IFT57 hypomorphic splice mutation
checks.explanation: The paper links a homozygous IFT57 mutation to an unclassified OFDS. The label OFD18 is OMIM's name for this disorder, not the paper's.

checks.claim: The IFT57 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.12-q13.13.
checks.evidence_quote: namely an IFT57 synonymous variation (chr3:g.107910368C>T, c.777G>A, p.Lys259Lys, RefSeq accession number NM_018010.3)
checks.explanation: The paper places the variant on chromosome 3. The cytogenetic band is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is an autosomal recessive ciliopathy (Thevenon et al., 2016). The orofaciodigital syndromes are a heterogeneous group of disorders that share malformations of the oral cavity, face, and digits (Phadke et al., 1999). These can include oral frenulae, cleft lip and/or palate, and polydactyly (Thevenon et al., 2016).

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive IFT57 hypomorphic mutation cause ciliary transport defect in unclassified oral-facial-digital syndrome with short stature and brachymesophalangia.
checks.explanation: The paper's title states autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is a ciliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS, extending the genetic heterogeneity of this subgroup of ciliopathies.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as a ciliopathy with a ciliary transport defect.

checks.claim: The orofaciodigital syndromes are a heterogeneous group of disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: The Oral-Facial-Digital syndromes (OFDS) are a heterogeneous group of disorders having common oral, facial, and digital malformations.
checks.explanation: The abstract says outright that the OFDS are a heterogeneous group of disorders.

checks.claim: The orofaciodigital syndromes share malformations of the oral cavity, face, and digits.
checks.evidence_quote: The Oral-Facial-Digital syndromes (OFDS) are a heterogeneous group of disorders having common oral, facial, and digital malformations.
checks.explanation: The abstract's "common oral, facial, and digital malformations" is the same claim as shared malformations of the oral cavity, face and digits.

checks.claim: Malformations in the orofaciodigital syndromes can include oral frenulae.
checks.evidence_quote: i) oral anomalies such as tongue hamartomas, oral frenulae, cleft palate, abnormal teething
checks.explanation: Oral frenulae are listed among the OFDS features.

checks.claim: Malformations in the orofaciodigital syndromes can include cleft lip and/or palate.
checks.evidence_quote: oral frenulae, cleft palate, abnormal teething; ii) facial dysmorphism such as hypertelorism, lateral or medial cleft lip
checks.explanation: Cleft palate and cleft lip are both listed.

checks.claim: Malformations in the orofaciodigital syndromes can include polydactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: iii) digital anomalies such as pre-, meso- or post-axial polydactyly, abnormal Y-shaped metacarpes, or syndactylies
checks.explanation: Polydactyly is listed among the digital anomalies.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) found a homozygous IFT57 mutation in a consanguineous family with OFD18, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) found a homozygous IFT57 mutation in a family with OFD18.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing led to the identification of a homozygous mutation in IFT57
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous IFT57 mutation in the family.

checks.claim: The family with OFD18 studied by Thevenon et al. (2016) was consanguineous.
checks.evidence_quote: A unique consanguineous family presenting with an unclassified OFDS with skeletal dysplasia and brachymesophalangia was explored.
checks.explanation: The paper states the family is consanguineous.

checks.claim: The homozygous IFT57 mutation in a consanguineous family with OFD18 is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive IFT57 hypomorphic mutation cause ciliary transport defect in unclassified oral-facial-digital syndrome
checks.explanation: The paper describes the mutation as autosomal recessive, found homozygous in a consanguineous family.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) noted that the orofaciodigital syndromes are genetically heterogeneous, and that most of the known causal genes encode proteins that act at the primary cilium or the centrosome.

checks.claim: The orofaciodigital syndromes are genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, an unclassified type of OFDS was evoked, once more underlying the clinical and genetic heterogeneity of OFDS.
checks.explanation: The paper explicitly notes the genetic heterogeneity of OFDS.

checks.claim: Most of the known genes causing orofaciodigital syndromes encode proteins that act at the primary cilium or the centrosome.
checks.evidence_quote: While most OFDS are ciliopathies caused by mutated centrosomal proteins (OFD1, SCLT1 and TBC1D32/C6orf170) or components of the transition zone (TMEM216 and TCNT3).
checks.explanation: The paper names centrosomal proteins and transition-zone components. The draft's 'act at the primary cilium or the centrosome' is a close but not exact paraphrase.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in a consanguineous family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype. They identified a homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene, which encodes a component of intraflagellar transport complex B. Thevenon et al. (2016) concluded that this finding tied the disorder to defective ciliary intraflagellar transport.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in a family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing was performed on Subject II-1 (Figure 1A) according to standard procedures using the Nimblegen SeqCap EZ Exome v2.0 kit
checks.explanation: The paper reports exome sequencing in the family.

checks.claim: The family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype studied by Thevenon et al. (2016) by whole-exome sequencing was consanguineous.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering the parental consanguinity, homozygosity regions were screened using homozygosity mapping in subjects 1 and 2.
checks.explanation: The paper notes the parents are consanguineous.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) identified a homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene in the consanguineous family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the variation at a homozygous status in the 3 affected subjects.
checks.explanation: The IFT57 variant was homozygous in all three affected siblings.

checks.claim: The IFT57 gene encodes a component of intraflagellar transport complex B.
checks.evidence_quote: However, further analysis indicated that IFT57 is a subunit of intraflagellar transport complex B.
checks.explanation: The paper states IFT57 is a subunit of IFT complex B.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) concluded that the homozygous IFT57 mutation tied orofaciodigital syndrome to defective ciliary intraflagellar transport.
checks.evidence_quote: This report identifies the implication of IFT57 in human pathology and highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS
checks.explanation: The paper concludes the mutation causes a ciliary transport defect in OFDS.
